factual_methodology.summary: Primary evidence comes from the Federal Reserve, ECB, Bank of England, IMF, Basel Committee and BIS. The FOMC minutes are explicitly treated as scheduled rather than released at the information cutoff.

novelty.summary: Updates the institutional line from late-September decisions to the October operating agenda: IMF surveillance reform, machine-readable Basel disclosure and AI-agent payments alongside still-restrictive policy rates.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Public prose states facts and mechanisms directly, separates observed evidence from inference, includes explicit limitations and contains no internal publication-process narration.

contextual_depth.summary: Connects policy rates, balance-sheet transmission, surveillance, disclosure architecture and agentic payment governance without conflating them.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Required visual budget and EN/PT-BR visual parity were checked; quantitative visuals use compatible units and structural visuals encode mechanisms defended in prose.

contrary_evidence: The report is published before the 7 October FOMC minutes release and does not infer their content.
Policy-rate levels are not directly comparable measures of tightness across jurisdictions.
limitations: The report is published before the 7 October FOMC minutes release and does not infer their content.
Policy-rate levels are not directly comparable measures of tightness across jurisdictions.
AI-agent payment governance is an emerging institutional agenda, not evidence of economy-wide autonomous payment adoption.
notes: Approved in the 7 October deep editorial refresh after source, bilingual, taxonomy and visual checks.

en.title: Global Monetary Institutions — rates remain restrictive while surveillance, disclosure and AI governance move into the operating agenda
en.deck: Major central banks remain restrictive while the IMF, Basel Committee and Federal Reserve expand the institutional agenda toward risk-based surveillance, machine-readable disclosure and AI-agent payments.
en.regime: Restrictive policy rates coexist with an institutional shift toward risk-based surveillance, machine-readable prudential disclosure and governance of AI-mediated financial activity.
en.key_risk: Institutions may face faster and more correlated financial adjustment before their disclosure, monitoring and intervention frameworks adapt to increasingly automated markets and payments.

pt-BR.title: Instituições Monetárias Globais — juros seguem restritivos enquanto supervisão, divulgação e governança de IA entram na agenda operacional
pt-BR.deck: Grandes bancos centrais seguem restritivos enquanto FMI, Comitê de Basileia e Federal Reserve ampliam a agenda para supervisão orientada a risco, divulgação legível por máquinas e pagamentos por agentes de IA.
pt-BR.regime: Juros restritivos coexistem com deslocamento institucional para supervisão orientada a risco, divulgação prudencial legível por máquinas e governança de atividade financeira mediada por IA.
pt-BR.key_risk: Instituições podem enfrentar ajustes financeiros mais rápidos e correlacionados antes que divulgação, monitoramento e instrumentos de intervenção se adaptem a mercados e pagamentos automatizados.
